mainTopic: The end of דרכי האמורי and פרק במה אשה, and the opening משנה of כלל גדול on counting חטאות for mistaken שבת labor
overview: The גמרא finishes its list of דרכי האמורי, the superstitious customs of the nations that a Jew may not copy. The list includes lucky sayings like 'גד גדי' and 'דונו דני', talking to ravens, killing a chicken because of its odd crowing, and rituals done for chicks or for cooking. רבי יהודה says the sayings with 'גד' and 'דן' are worse than superstition: they are actual עבודה זרה, because those words are names of idols in פסוקים. The test throughout is the method. A trick that really works, like putting mulberry wood in a pot or salt in a lamp, is allowed. חכמים forbid glass shards in a pot only because of danger. רב זוטרא adds that making lamp fuel burn faster for no reason violates בל תשחית. The toast 'חמרא וחיי לפום רבנן' is permitted, as shown by רבי עקיבא at his son's feast. Then פרק במה אשה ends, and פרק כלל גדול opens with a משנה about how many חטאות someone brings for doing labors on שבת by mistake. The answer depends on the kind of mistake, and the משנה's third case continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Blessing your fortune with 'גד גדי'
steps.stepSummary: Saying 'גד גדי' to bless one's luck is forbidden as דרכי האמורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who says, 'My fortune, be fortunate, and do not grow tired by day or by night,' is doing something that falls under דרכי האמורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new case from the list of דרכי האמורי. Calling on your 'fortune' to stay strong is a forbidden superstitious practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person is speaking to their 'luck' (גד) as if it were a power that can be asked to keep working for them. The תנא קמא treats this as superstition, the kind of practice the nations have. That puts it in the category of דרכי האמורי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'My fortune, be fortunate' — speaking to one's luck
It contains an element of / it falls under the prohibition of
'Ways of the Amorite' — forbidden superstitious practices of the nations

phrases.english: One who says: 'My fortune, be fortunate,'
phrases.notes: גד here means 'fortune' or 'luck'.

phrases.english: 'and do not grow weary by day or by night' —
phrases.notes: Aramaic words asking the 'fortune' to stay active at all times.

phrases.english: it contains an element of the ways of the Amorite.
phrases.notes: This is the standard formula repeated for every case in this list.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָאוֹמֵר ״גַּד גַּדִּי, וּסְנוּק לָא אַשְׁכִּי וּבוּשְׁכִּי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of דרכי האמורי cases from the earlier discussion on the daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying 'גד גדי' to one's fortune is prohibited as דרכי האמורי.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: 'גד' is the name of an idol
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says 'גד' is a term for עבודה זרה, which makes this case more severe. He proves it from a פסוק in ישעיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: 'גד' is nothing other than a word for עבודה זרה, as the פסוק says, 'Those who set a table for גד.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה adds a stricter view on the case from step 1. He holds that saying 'גד' is not just superstition but actually calling on an idol.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא called it דרכי האמורי. רבי יהודה says it is worse, because 'גד' is the name of a real idol. His proof is the פסוק in ישעיה (65:11), which criticizes people who 'set a table for גד', meaning they gave offerings to an idol named גד.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is said (introduces a פסוק)
'Those who set a table for גד' (ישעיה 65:11)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה is not being more lenient. He agrees the saying is forbidden. He only argues that it is even more serious: actual עבודה זרה, not just דרכי האמורי.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
'Gad' is nothing other than a term of idolatry,
as it is stated: 'Those who set a table for Gad' (Isaiah 65:11).
phrases.notes: Setting a table means bringing food offerings to an idol.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: ״גַּד״ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a stricter view of the same case. The same act is moved into the more severe category of עבודה זרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, saying 'גד גדי' is calling on an idol, which is עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Husband and wife swapping names
steps.stepSummary: Calling a husband by his wife's name and the wife by his name, for good luck, is דרכי האמורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he is called by her name and she is called by his name, for good fortune, that falls under דרכי האמורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists another forbidden superstitious practice: a couple swapping names to bring good luck.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Changing names here has no real purpose. It is done only because people believe it brings luck or protects the couple. That belief-based act is exactly what דרכי האמורי forbids.

phrases.english: He by her name and she by his name —
phrases.notes: A couple calls each other by the other's name for good fortune.

phrases.english: it contains an element of the ways of the Amorite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the list and adds a new, separate case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband and wife swapping names for good luck is prohibited as דרכי האמורי.

steps.title: Saying 'דונו דני' over barrels
steps.stepSummary: Saying 'דונו דני' ('let my barrels be strong') is דרכי האמורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who says 'דונו דני' — 'Let my barrels be strengthened' — is doing something that falls under דרכי האמורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another magic-like saying. This one is said over wine barrels so they will stay strong or full.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are a charm meant to protect one's barrels. They have no natural effect. Because the saying works only as a superstition, the תנא קמא counts it as דרכי האמורי.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Let my barrels be strengthened' — a charm over wine barrels

phrases.english: 'Let my barrels be strengthened' —
phrases.notes: דני means barrels or jugs.

phrases.english: it contains an element of the ways of the Amorite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new case to the list, and it follows the same pattern as the גד case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying 'דונו דני' is prohibited as דרכי האמורי.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: 'דן' is the name of an idol
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה says 'דן' is a term for עבודה זרה. He proves it from a פסוק in עמוס.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: 'דן' is nothing other than a word for עבודה זרה, as the פסוק says, 'Those who swear by the guilt of שומרון and say: As your god, דן, lives.'
steps.whatsHappening: Just like with 'גד', רבי יהודה says the word 'דן' in this saying refers to an idol. That makes the saying actual עבודה זרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in עמוס (8:14) describes people swearing by 'your god, דן'. This refers to the idol (the golden calf) that ירבעם set up in the city of דן. Since 'דן' was used as an idol's name, saying 'דונו דני' sounds like calling on that idol. This step follows the same pattern as step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The guilt of שומרון' — the idol worship of the northern kingdom
'As your god, דן, lives' — swearing by an idol

steps.confusionAlert: 'גד' and 'דן' here are not the שבטים (tribes). In these sayings they are used as names of idols. 'דן' refers to the idol that was worshipped in the city of דן.
steps.whatToRemember: The pattern: the תנא קמא calls these sayings דרכי האמורי (superstition). רבי יהודה says that when the saying contains a name like גד or דן, it is actually calling on an idol, which is עבודה זרה. He proves each one from a פסוק.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
'Dan' is nothing other than a term of idolatry,
as it is stated: 'Those who swear by the guilt of Samaria
phrases.notes: עמוס 8:14.

phrases.english: and say: As your god, Dan, lives.'
phrases.notes: Refers to the calf idol set up in the city of דן.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵין ״דָּן״ אֶלָּא לְשׁוֹן עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יהודה's stricter view on step 4, in the same way he ruled on גד in step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, saying 'דונו דני' is calling on an idol, which is עבודה זרה.

steps.title: Talking to a raven to avoid a bad omen
steps.stepSummary: Speaking to a male or female raven so that its call becomes a good sign is דרכי האמורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who says to a male raven, 'Scream!', and to a female raven, 'Whistle, and turn your tail back to me for good!', is doing something that falls under דרכי האמורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists one more superstitious practice. A person hears a raven, worries it is a bad sign, and talks to the bird to turn it into a good sign.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People believed a raven's call was an omen, meaning a sign of what will happen. Speaking to the bird to change the omen treats the raven as a source of fate. That is a classic act of דרכי האמורי.

keyTerms.meaning: For good / for a good outcome

steps.whyThisMatters: This case shows that דרכי האמורי includes believing in signs (omens) from animals and trying to control them. This connects to the broader איסור against relying on omens.

phrases.english: One who says to a raven: 'Scream,'
and to a female raven: 'Whistle
and turn your tail back to me for good' —
phrases.notes: Asking the bird to make its omen a good one.

phrases.english: it contains an element of the ways of the Amorite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another separate case to the list of דרכי האמורי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Talking to ravens to change an omen into a good one is prohibited as דרכי האמורי.

steps.title: Slaughtering a chicken because of strange crowing
steps.stepSummary: Saying 'slaughter this rooster that crowed in the evening' or 'this hen that crowed like a rooster' is דרכי האמורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who says, 'Slaughter this rooster because it crowed in the evening,' or 'Slaughter this hen because it crowed like a rooster,' is doing something that falls under דרכי האמורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another item to the list of superstitious practices. Treating a chicken's unusual crowing as a bad sign and killing it to stop the bad luck is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unusual crowing was seen as an omen of bad luck. Killing the bird to cancel that omen is the problem, because the action is based on superstition and not on any real reason. This fits the pattern of the earlier items: doing or saying something because of a 'sign.'

keyTerms.meaning: 'Ways of the Amorite': forbidden superstitious customs of the nations
Like a male, meaning a rooster's crow

steps.confusionAlert: Slaughtering a chicken is not the problem. The problem is slaughtering it because you think its crowing is a bad omen.

phrases.english: One who says: 'Slaughter this rooster'
'that crowed in the evening'
phrases.notes: Crowing at an unusual time was seen as a bad sign.

phrases.english: and 'this hen that crowed like a rooster'
this falls under the ways of the Amorite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of דרכי האמורי examples after the raven case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Killing a chicken to cancel the 'omen' of its odd crowing is דרכי האמורי.

steps.title: A lucky phrase while drinking wine
steps.stepSummary: Saying 'I will drink and leave over' so that the wine will increase is דרכי האמורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who says, 'I will drink and leave some over, I will drink and leave some over,' is doing something that falls under דרכי האמורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lists another superstitious saying. Repeating a phrase as a charm so your wine supply will grow is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving wine over is not the issue. The issue is chanting the words as a magic formula, hoping the speech itself will make the wine multiply. This is like 'דונו דני' earlier, a lucky saying about wine barrels.

phrases.english: 'I will drink and leave over, I will drink and leave over'
phrases.notes: Said repeatedly as a charm for having more wine.

phrases.english: this falls under the ways of the Amorite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another item in the same list. It moves from actions with animals to a lucky phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Chanting a phrase so your wine will increase is דרכי האמורי.

steps.title: Cracking eggs on a wall in front of chicks
steps.stepSummary: A woman who cracks eggs on a wall and smears them in front of the chicks is doing דרכי האמורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who cracks eggs against a wall and smears them in front of the young chicks is doing something that falls under דרכי האמורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now lists a superstitious action rather than a saying. Smashing eggs on a wall in front of chicks, as a ritual to protect them, is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The action has no practical purpose. It was done as a charm so the chicks would survive and grow. Because the act relies on magic and not on any real cause, it counts as דרכי האמורי.

phrases.english: A woman who cracks eggs on a wall
and smears them in front of the chicks
this falls under the ways of the Amorite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list and switches from sayings to ritual actions involving chicks.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Cracking and smearing eggs in front of chicks as a charm is דרכי האמורי.

steps.title: Stirring a pot in front of chicks
steps.stepSummary: Stirring a pot in front of chicks for good luck is דרכי האמורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone who stirs a pot in front of the chicks, so that they will not die, is doing something that falls under דרכי האמורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives one more action involving chicks. Stirring a pot in front of them as a protective ritual is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stirring a pot is a normal kitchen act. Doing it in front of chicks as a charm for their survival turns it into superstition. This pairs with the previous step, since both are rituals meant to protect chicks.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule behind every item on this list is the same. If a saying or action is done because people believe it magically brings luck, with no real natural reason behind it, it falls under דרכי האמורי.

phrases.english: And one who stirs a pot in front of chicks
this falls under the ways of the Amorite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pairs with step 9 as a second ritual meant to protect chicks.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Stirring a pot in front of chicks as a charm is דרכי האמורי.

steps.title: Dancing and counting seventy-one chicks
steps.stepSummary: A woman who dances and counts 71 chicks so they will not die is doing דרכי האמורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who dances, and counts seventy-one chicks so that they won't die, is doing something that falls under דרכי האמורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The list of forbidden superstitions continues with another chicken-raising practice. Dancing and counting to a set number of chicks, hoping this keeps them alive, is labeled דרכי האמורי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the earlier items about chicks, there is no natural connection between dancing or counting and the chicks surviving. Because it is pure 'magic thinking,' it is classed as copying the superstitious customs of the nations.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Ways of the Amorite.' Superstitious non-Jewish customs that a Jew may not practice.

phrases.english: A woman who dances, and who counts
phrases.notes: Read here as one combined action: she dances while counting the chicks.

phrases.english: seventy-one chicks
so that they will not die
it contains an element of the ways of the Amorite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of chick-related superstitions from steps 9 and 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dancing and counting 71 chicks to keep them alive is דרכי האמורי.

steps.title: Dancing, silencing, and screaming for successful cooking
steps.stepSummary: Dancing for the כותח, silencing people for lentils, and screaming for split grain are all דרכי האמורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who dances so the כותח will turn out well, a woman who makes people be quiet so the lentils will cook well, and a woman who shouts so the split grain will cook well are all doing דרכי האמורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The list moves from chicks to the kitchen. Three cooking 'tricks' that are really just superstitions are all labeled דרכי האמורי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each action (dancing, silence, shouting) has nothing to do with how food actually cooks. The point stays the same as before: an action done for luck, with no real cause-and-effect, is forbidden as דרכי האמורי.

keyTerms.meaning: A dip or relish made from bread, whey, and salt
A woman who makes others be silent
A woman who screams or shouts
Split or crushed grain, like pearl barley or groats

phrases.english: A woman who dances for the kutach,
phrases.notes: She dances so that it will turn out well.

phrases.english: and one who silences people for the lentils,
and one who screams for the split grain
it contains an element of the ways of the Amorite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list, shifting from chick-raising to cooking superstitions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dancing, silencing, or screaming to make food come out well is דרכי האמורי.

steps.title: Urinating in front of a pot to speed cooking
steps.stepSummary: Urinating in front of one's pot so it cooks quickly is דרכי האמורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A woman who urinates in front of her pot so that it will cook quickly is doing something that falls under דרכי האמורי.
steps.whatsHappening: This is one more kitchen superstition, aimed at making food cook faster. It is also labeled דרכי האמורי. It sets up the contrast in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goal here (faster cooking) is exactly the same as the goal in the next step. The difference is the method: here it has no real effect, so it is superstition. This is what makes the next step's contrast so sharp.

phrases.english: A woman who urinates in front of her pot
so that it will cook quickly
it contains an element of the ways of the Amorite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the cooking superstitions and introduces the goal of fast cooking, which the next step contrasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Urinating before a pot to hasten cooking is דרכי האמורי.

steps.title: Permitted: mulberry wood and glass to speed cooking
steps.stepSummary: But it is allowed to put a mulberry chip and glass shards into a pot to make it cook faster.
steps.simpleTranslation: However, one may put a splinter of mulberry wood and pieces of glass into a pot so that it will cook quickly.
steps.whatsHappening: The word אבל ('but') turns the list around. For the same goal of fast cooking, putting mulberry wood or glass into the pot is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mulberry wood and glass actually help the food soften and cook, so this is a real, natural method and not magic. This fits the principle taught earlier in the סוגיא: something that truly works (like רפואה) is not דרכי האמורי.

keyTerms.meaning: But, however. It signals a contrast with what came before.
A splinter or chip of wood

steps.whatToRemember: The test for דרכי האמורי is not the goal but the method. A method with a real, natural effect is allowed. A method that works only 'by luck' is forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think fast cooking itself is the problem. Steps 13 and 14 have the same goal. Only the method (superstition versus a real effect) decides the הלכה.

phrases.english: But one may put a chip of mulberry wood
and shards of glass into the pot
so that it will cook quickly,
phrases.notes: These are allowed because they have a real effect on the cooking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 13. The goal is the same, but the method is natural and therefore permitted.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Putting mulberry wood or glass shards in a pot to speed cooking is permitted, because it has a real effect.

steps.title: The Sages forbid glass because of danger
steps.stepSummary: חכמים forbid the glass shards, not as superstition, but because of physical danger.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חכמים forbid the pieces of glass because of the danger.
steps.whatsHappening: חכמים disagree only about the glass. They forbid it because someone might swallow a sliver.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even חכמים agree that the glass is not דרכי האמורי, since it really works. Their ban comes from a completely different category: protecting people from harm (סכנה). The mulberry wood stays permitted according to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Danger, a physical risk to health

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that one thing can be allowed under one category (it is not superstition) and still be forbidden under a different one (danger). Each concern has to be checked separately.

phrases.english: And the Sages forbid the shards of glass
because of the danger.
phrases.notes: Someone might swallow a sliver of glass left in the food.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the permission of step 14 for glass only, using a different concern (danger) rather than superstition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Glass shards are forbidden in a pot because of physical danger, though not as דרכי האמורי.

steps.title: Salt and clay may be used to improve a lamp
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא permits putting salt into a lamp so it burns brighter, and mud or clay under it so it burns longer.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: You may put a lump of salt into a lamp so it will shine brightly. You may also put mud or clay under a lamp so it will burn slowly and last longer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא listing lamp tricks that are allowed because they actually work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the mulberry chip in step 14, these are real physical methods, not magic. So they are not דרכי האמורי. The salt makes the flame brighter, and the clay underneath keeps the oil cool so it burns more slowly.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נוֹתְנִין בּוּל שֶׁל מֶלַח
phrases.english: The Sages taught: One may put a lump of salt
into a lamp so that it will shine and burn
And one may put mud and clay under the lamp
so that it will burn slowly and keep burning
phrases.notes: The cool clay slows the burning of the oil.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: נוֹתְנִין בּוּל שֶׁל מֶלַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of practical, permitted actions that are not דרכי האמורי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Practical, effective lamp techniques are permitted and are not דרכי האמורי.

steps.title: Wasting lamp fuel violates the ban on needless destruction
steps.stepSummary: רב זוטרא says that covering an oil lamp or uncovering a naphtha lamp needlessly makes the fuel burn faster, which violates בל תשחית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב זוטרא said: A person who covers an oil lamp, or uncovers a naphtha lamp, transgresses the prohibition of בל תשחית (wasteful destruction).
steps.whatsHappening: After discussing how to make a lamp last longer, רב זוטרא adds the opposite case: making it burn faster for no reason is forbidden waste.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Covering an oil lamp traps heat and makes the oil burn quickly. Naphtha burns away fast when it is left uncovered. Either way, fuel is wasted for no purpose, and that falls under בל תשחית.

keyTerms.meaning: The prohibition against needless destruction or waste

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that בל תשחית applies even to small, everyday waste, like fuel burning up for no reason.

phrases.english: Rav Zutra said: One who
covers an oil lamp
phrases.notes: Covering traps heat, so the oil burns faster.

phrases.english: or uncovers a naphtha lamp
transgresses the prohibition of 'Do not destroy'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב זוּטְרָא: הַאי מַאן דִּמְכַסֵּי שְׁרָגָא דְּמִשְׁחָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A related side-ruling: after making lamps last longer, the גמרא forbids making them burn faster needlessly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Needlessly making lamp fuel burn faster violates בל תשחית.

steps.title: The toast 'wine and life to the Sages' is permitted
steps.stepSummary: Saying 'חמרא וחיי לפום רבנן' over wine is not considered דרכי האמורי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Saying 'Wine and life to the mouth of the Sages' is not included in דרכי האמורי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the topic of דרכי האמורי and permits a common toast said over wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think a set formula said over wine is a superstitious charm. The גמרא rules that it is not. It is simply a blessing and a mark of respect for תלמידי חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: To the mouth of the Sages
Ways of the Amorites; forbidden superstitious practices

phrases.english: 'Wine and life to the mouth of the Sages'
is not considered the ways of the Amorites

steps.triggerLanguage: חַמְרָא וְחַיֵּי לְפוּם רַבָּנַן אֵין בּוֹ מִשּׁוּם דַּרְכֵי הָאֱמוֹרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the בל תשחית side-point to the list of what is and is not דרכי האמורי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The toast 'חמרא וחיי לפום רבנן' is permitted and is not superstition.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא said this toast at his son's feast
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא made a feast for his son and said the toast over every cup, adding 'and to the mouth of their students'.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story with רבי עקיבא, who made a feast for his son. Over every cup of wine he brought, he said: 'Wine and life to the mouth of the Sages; life and wine to the mouth of the Sages and to the mouth of their students.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about רבי עקיבא to support the ruling that this toast is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a גדול like רבי עקיבא said this toast again and again, it clearly is not a forbidden superstition. He even expanded it to include the students, which shows it is a blessing of honor for Torah learners.

keyTerms.meaning: An incident or story brought as support

steps.whatToRemember: Practical actions that really work, and blessings of honor like 'חמרא וחיי לפום רבנן', are not דרכי האמורי. Only acts that rely on superstition are forbidden.

phrases.english: There was an incident with Rabbi Akiva
who made a feast for his son

phrases.aramaic: וְעַל כׇּל כּוֹס וָכוֹס שֶׁהֵבִיא אָמַר:
phrases.english: and over each and every cup that he brought, he said:
'Wine and life to the mouth of the Sages;
life and wine to the mouth of the Sages
and to the mouth of their students.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא שֶׁעָשָׂה מִשְׁתֶּה לִבְנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports step 18 with a story about how a great Sage behaved.
steps.raayaObject: That the toast 'חמרא וחיי לפום רבנן' is permitted.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי עקיבא's practice at his son's feast.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing the chapter of במה אשה
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula marks the end of the sixth chapter of שבת, פרק במה אשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק במה אשה.
steps.whatsHappening: This line ends the chapter. It is not part of the argument; it is the traditional farewell to a completed פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן expresses a wish to return and learn this chapter again. פרק במה אשה dealt with what a woman (and others) may wear or carry out on שבת, and it closed with a long section on remedies and דרכי האמורי.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (the closing formula for a chapter)
'With what may a woman [go out]' — the name of the chapter

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'With what may a woman'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the chapter after its final discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The sixth chapter of מסכת שבת, פרק במה אשה, is complete.

steps.title: New chapter: one who forgot the essence of שבת brings only one offering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה opens פרק כלל גדול. Someone who totally forgot about שבת and did many forbidden labors over many שבתות brings only one חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The Sages stated a big rule about שבת. Anyone who forgot the basic idea of שבת, and did many forbidden labors over many שבתות, brings only one sin-offering.
steps.whatsHappening: A new chapter starts with a משנה. It gives the first of three cases: a person who forgot that שבת even exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת is brought for a sin done by mistake, and the number of offerings depends on how many separate mistakes there were. Here there was really only one mistake: the person did not know about שבת at all. So even many labors on many שבתות count as one long error, and he brings one חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; the text the גמרא is about to discuss
A big rule; also the name of this chapter
The basic idea of שבת, that the Torah forbids work on that day
A sin-offering brought for certain sins done by mistake
Someone who sins by mistake, without knowing

steps.confusionAlert: The person in this case is not someone who meant to sin. All three cases in this משנה are about mistakes. The question is only how many offerings the mistake requires.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole chapter's main question: what makes sins count as separate, so that each one needs its own חטאת?

phrases.english: MISHNA: They stated a great principle with regard to Shabbat:
phrases.notes: Opening words of the new chapter, which is named after them.

phrases.english: anyone who forgets the essence of Shabbat,
phrases.notes: For example, someone who never knew or completely forgot that there is a מצוה of שבת.

phrases.english: and performed many labors on many Shabbatot,
is liable to bring only one sin-offering.
phrases.notes: It counts as one mistake, so one offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new chapter right after the Hadran that closed פרק במה אשה in step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who forgot the essence of שבת brings a single חטאת for all his labors on all the שבתות.

steps.title: One who knew about שבת but lost track of the days brings an offering for each שבת
steps.stepSummary: Second case: the person knew about שבת but did not realize those days were שבת. He brings a separate חטאת for each שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who knew the basic idea of שבת, and did many forbidden labors over many שבתות, is liable for each and every שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the second case. This person knew that שבת exists but made a mistake about which days were שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the mistake is about the day, not about שבת itself. Each שבת he lost track of counts as its own mistake, so he brings one חטאת for each שבת. But within one שבת, all his labors still count together as one.

keyTerms.meaning: Each and every שבת; one offering for each
Labors; the kinds of work forbidden on שבת

phrases.english: One who knows the essence of Shabbat,
phrases.notes: He knows שבת exists but forgot that a certain day was שבת.

phrases.english: and performed many labors on many Shabbatot,
is liable for each and every Shabbat.
phrases.notes: One חטאת per שבת, no matter how many labors were done on it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second case that contrasts with step 21. Knowing about שבת turns each שבת into a separate mistake.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who knows the essence of שבת but forgot the day brings a חטאת for each שבת.

steps.title: One who knew it was שבת but not that the labors were forbidden
steps.stepSummary: Third case: the person knew the day was שבת but did not know these labors were forbidden. The text breaks off as the משנה starts to say he is liable for each one.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who knew that it was שבת, and did many forbidden labors over many שבתות, is liable for each... (the sentence continues on the next amud: each main category of labor).
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה begins its third case. This person knew the day was שבת, but his mistake was about the law: he did not know these kinds of work are forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the mistake is about each type of work, so every main category of labor counts as its own mistake. That makes this the strictest of the three cases. The amud ends at "חייב על כל", and the next amud finishes the sentence with each אב מלאכה.

keyTerms.meaning: That it is שבת; he knows today is שבת
A main category of forbidden labor (the next words of the משנה)
Aware it is שבת but mistaken about which labors are forbidden

steps.whatToRemember: Three cases, three different counts: forgot שבת itself → one חטאת; forgot the day → one per שבת; forgot the labors are forbidden → one per type of labor. The count follows the kind of mistake.

phrases.english: One who knows that it is Shabbat,
phrases.notes: He knows the day, but not that these labors are forbidden.

phrases.english: and performed many labors on many Shabbatot,
is liable for each…
phrases.notes: The sentence is cut off here. It continues on the next amud: "אב מלאכה ומלאכה", each main category of labor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third and strictest case, following steps 21 and 22. The mistake is now about the labors themselves.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who knows it is שבת but is mistaken about the labors is liable for each labor (finished on the next amud: for each אב מלאכה).
